property_summary: For any call to the fallback, if it does not revert then the value transferred must be exactly 10 ether; the mutant allows success with 0 ether, violating the invariant that successful fallback calls require msg.value == 10 ether.

After any successful call to the fallback with msg.value == 0 ether, the contract's pastBlockTime must not have been updated; the buggy version updates it, allowing a successful 0-ether call to change the state.

After any external call to the fallback, if msg.value is not exactly 10 ether, the call must revert; the mutant allows a non-reverting fallback call with msg.value == 0 ether, breaking the invariant that only exactly 10 ether transfers succeed.
Any successful call to fallback must have msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant succeeds with 0 ether, violating this invariant.
Any non-reverting call to the fallback must have msg.value == 10 ether; the mutant succeeds with 0 ether.
A call to the fallback function with any value less than or equal to 10 ether must succeed without reverting, which the reference always does but the mutant reverts for values exactly 10 ether.

For any call to the fallback with at least 10 ether, if the call does not revert, the pastBlockTime must be updated to the current block timestamp; in the reference this always holds (since exactly 10 ether succeeds), but the buggy version reverts for 10 ether and thus fails to update pastBlockTime on some admissible inputs.

A payable fallback call with any value will revert if and only if msg.value is not exactly 10 ether in the reference, but the mutant reverts for msg.value > 10 ether, breaking that symmetry — so whenever a call with value > 10 ether succeeds, the pastBlockTime must have been updated.

For any payable fallback call with any value, if the call succeeds then exactly 10 ether (the reference requirement) OR more than 10 ether (the mutant requirement) must have been sent; the reference succeeds only for exactly 10 ether, while the mutant succeeds only for >10 ether, so there is no shared success value.

For any call to the fallback, if the call succeeds and the balance of C is non-zero afterward, then block.timestamp must be strictly greater than c.pastBlockTime(); the reference always satisfies this because only exactly 10 ether calls succeed, but the mutant allows >10 ether calls to succeed without updating pastBlockTime when block.number % 15 != 0, leaving pastBlockTime unchanged while balance becomes non-zero, violating the invariant.
The reference contract always updates pastBlockTime on a valid call, so a second valid call never reverts due to the timelock check; the mutant never updates it, so the second valid call will revert.

For any sequence of valid fallback calls, the reference contract never reverts on a later call due to the `require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime)` check because it always updates `pastBlockTime`, whereas the mutant reverts on the second valid call because `pastBlockTime` remains at its initial zero value after the first call, so `block.timestamp > 0` fails when `block.timestamp` is 0.

For any sequence of two valid fallback calls where block.timestamp increases to a nonzero value after the first call, the reference contract succeeds on the second call, but the mutant reverts because pastBlockTime is never updated.

For any valid fallback call with 10 ether, the reference contract updates pastBlockTime to the current block.timestamp, so a subsequent valid call cannot revert due to the require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) check; the mutant never updates pastBlockTime, so a second valid call reverts if block.timestamp has not advanced past the first call's timestamp.

For any admissible fallback call with 10 ether sent from an EOA, the reference contract's balance should remain unchanged (since conditional transfers may or may not happen), but the buggy version's balance strictly increases by exactly 10 ether every time—thus the invariant 'after a valid fallback call, the contract's Ether balance is always equal to the initial balance plus 10 ether' holds for the buggy version but fails for the reference when the if-condition is true.

For any admissible fallback call (10 ether, strictly increasing block.timestamp), the reference contract's balance never exceeds the total Ether it has received, but the buggy contract's balance always equals exactly the received amount.
After a valid fallback call, the contract's balance can decrease only when block.number % 15 == 0; the buggy version never decreases its balance.

For any admissible fallback call, the contract's pastBlockTime always equals the block.timestamp after the call, but the buggy version's pastBlockTime remains 0 after a reverted transfer to a contract that consumes all gas, violating the invariant.

After any valid fallback call, if the transfer condition is met (block.number % 15 == 0), the reference contract's balance is emptied while the buggy version retains all received ether, so an invariant that the contract's post-call balance plus any transfer to the caller equals the pre-call balance plus 10 ether holds for reference but fails for the mutant.
